title: Internship 101
description: During the training, key aspects related to the hiring process were covered at a high level. It started with explaining the terminology used in job postings and how to properly understand specific requirements. The recruitment process within a company was also presented, highlighting the main steps a candidate goes through. There was a focus on how academic activities – such as projects, laboratories, and volunteering – could be evaluated and turned into relevant experiences for a CV. Participants gained an overview of the basic skill sets required in fields such as electrical, mechanical, civil engineering, and IT. An important part of the session was dedicated to building an effective CV, covering structure, wording, and how to tailor it to a specific job. The training also included a practical exercise where participants, working in teams, created a CV for a fictional person. Finally, the “6 seconds rule” was discussed, emphasizing how to make a strong first impression from the very beginning.

title: Own Your Minute – Win the Interview
description: During the session, practical aspects related to interview behavior were also discussed. The participants were introduced to building a clear and compelling elevator pitch, under the concept of “Own Your Minute.” Examples of relevant and insightful questions that candidates can ask at the end of an interview were also provided. Emphasis was placed on maintaining the right attitude during the interview, including non-verbal communication, managing emotions, and active listening. Common mistakes encountered in interviews were highlighted, along with practical recommendations on how to avoid them. Depending on the available time, a short mock interview demonstration was also conducted.
